eso_milkyway_panorama.jpg.source: ESO, The Milky Way panorama (eso0932a), first image of the GigaGalaxy Zoom project, released 14 September 2009: ESO's 6000x3000 Large JPEG. The 800-megapixel original is not distributed by ESO.
eso_milkyway_panorama.jpg.licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, under ESO's image use terms (https://www.eso.org/public/outreach/copyright/): the credit stays unaltered and visible, and modifications must be indicated.
eso_milkyway_panorama.jpg.identification: Verified from the file's embedded ESO metadata (XMP): avm:ID eso0932a, avm:ReferenceURL https://www.eso.org/public/images/eso0932a/, photoshop:Credit ESO/S. Brunier, dc:title The Milky Way panorama, xmpRights:UsageTerms Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, avm:MetadataDate 2024-02-22. Not compared byte for byte with ESO's current download.
eso_milkyway_panorama.jpg.projection: Plate carree (equirectangular), 360 by 180 degrees, north galactic pole at the top and galactic longitude increasing to the left. ESO states only that the galactic plane runs horizontally. Measured against catalog stars, the image's axes sit 3.78 degrees from galactic: its centre is at l 3.23, b -1.69 and its top at l 330.83, b 88.00, with a 1.3 pixel vertical offset and stitching offsets of up to 2.2 texels (eso0932a_registration.json).
eso_milkyway_panorama.jpg.processing: None to the pixels. Both renderers sample the image by view direction through eso0932a_registration.json. The shader grades it for display: black level 0.042, power 1.52, a warm tint and a boost of its red excess (hAlphaKnots).
eso_milkyway_panorama.jpg.note: A mosaic of almost 300 fields, each shot four times (nearly 1,200 photos) over 2008 and 2009 and stitched by Frederic Tapissier. It shows two planets where they stood when their fields were shot: Venus at RA 23h19m, Dec -3.9, and Jupiter at RA 19h30m, Dec -21.9. The repo's ephemeris puts Venus within 0.07 degrees of that point on 2009-01-22 and Jupiter within 0.06 degrees on 2008-06-09. Those are dates of agreement, not capture dates from ESO.

eso0932a_registration.json.source: Fitted in this repository by scripts/register_sky_panorama.py from eso_milkyway_panorama.jpg (sha256 above) and the Gaia DR3 / Hipparcos 2007 catalog star tiles (apps/web/public/catalog/stars/gaia-dr3, layers 0 and 1).
eso0932a_registration.json.method: docs/science/SKY_PANORAMA_REGISTRATION.md: a rotation from galactic plus a vertical offset, then a smoothed table of the remaining offsets, fitted to 5,021 isolated stars to magnitude 6 and checked on held-out stars.
eso0932a_registration.json.credit: Catalog positions: Gaia DR3 (Gaia Collaboration 2023, ESA/Gaia/DPAC) and Hipparcos 2007 (van Leeuwen 2007).
eso0932a_registration.json.licence: Derived from ESA archive data distributed under CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO; commercial use needs ESA's authorisation (see the catalog manifest).
eso0932a_registration.json.processing: Regenerate with `uv run python scripts/register_sky_panorama.py`; `--verify` refits and compares byte for byte.

nasa_starmap_4k.jpg.source: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, Deep Star Maps: the celestial star map as a 1024x512 print JPEG. SVS offers that size and layout in both releases, as starmap_2020_4k_print.jpg (Deep Star Maps 2020, SVS 4851, plotted from Hipparcos-2, Tycho-2 and Gaia DR2) and starmap_4k_print.jpg (Deep Star Maps, 2012, SVS 3895). Which release this file is was not established.
nasa_starmap_4k.jpg.credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio. Gaia DR2: ESA/Gaia/DPAC (2020 release).
nasa_starmap_4k.jpg.licence: The SVS pages ask for the credit above and state no other terms. NASA's general media guidelines were not checked.
nasa_starmap_4k.jpg.identification: Inference, not verified: the file has no metadata. Its size, layout and look match the SVS print JPEGs: a plot of catalog stars with the Milky Way built from faint ones. It is not a photograph, and not ESO's panorama reprojected. Settling the release needs the SVS files downloaded and hashed.
nasa_starmap_4k.jpg.projection: Plate carree in ICRF/J2000 right ascension and declination, RA 0h at the centre and increasing to the left, north at the top, as the SVS 4851 caption states. Measured (tests/integration/test_sky_registration.py): 79 IAU-named stars to magnitude 2.5 sit a median 0.09 pixels (0.03 degrees) from their RA/Dec positions.
nasa_starmap_4k.jpg.processing: None to the pixels. Both renderers sample it by right ascension and declination. The shader grades it: black level 0.068, power 1.95, gain 0.72.
nasa_starmap_4k.jpg.note: The file name says 4k; the image is 1024x512. Every star it shows duplicates a catalog star the renderer draws from Gaia DR3 / Hipparcos 2007, and its Milky Way duplicates ESO's photograph, so removing it is proposed.
